chunks: Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who is given a garment to dye, but he ruins it.
So he عليه السلام said: Every worker whom you have given a wage to repair something, but he damages it instead, then he is liable.

key_terms.أَجْرًا: a wage or payment given for the work
key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: the garment that was entrusted for treatment or repair
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: legally liable and responsible for compensation
key_terms.عَامِلٍ: a worker or hired laborer performing a task
key_terms.لِيَصْبَغَهُ: to dye it; to perform a paid service on the item
key_terms.يُصْلِحَ: to repair, fix, or improve the item
key_terms.يُفْسِدُهُ: he ruins it or causes damage to it

ai.seo_question: Is a paid worker liable if he damages an item he was hired to repair?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes a legal ruling concerning hired labor: when a worker is paid to fix or improve an item but instead causes damage, he is financially liable for that damage. It reflects a principle of accountability in contractual work and the protection of others' property rights.
